_comment: Oracle for the nonshape_guards scenario. A @torch.compile function called with a changing python int arg `n`; dynamo specializes on the value and recompiles when it changes, with a guard `n == 1` — a raw boolean expression that carries NO expected/actual value (unlike a tensor shape/dtype/stride mismatch). torch appends a ` # <source> # <file>:<line>` comment after such guards; Mode A must strip it from the expression. Also exercises the `- User stack trace:` continuation lines that follow (skipped, not parsed as guards). This is the non-shape case the shape-only corpus was missing — the reason `failed_guard.previous_value`/`new_value` are Optional.
